newsitem.title: UK: BT weighs position on rival's poster ad.
newsitem.headline: BT weighs position on rival's poster ad.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Thursday said it has written to Bell Cablemedia Plc , a rival UK telephone service provider, about a poster advertisement it is running that highlights its price differential against BT and uses the slogan "British Telecon."
British Telecom said it is considering its position on the ad, but has not taken any legal action to date.

Bell Cablemedia, a cable television operator and phone service provider, launched a combined poster and radio advertising campaign on January 15. The ads are running in Bell Cablemedia's cable franchise areas in Britain.
The posters feature the the theme "Don't waste money -- switch to cable," as well as carrying the "British Telecon" slogan.
A BT spokesman told Reuters the company became aware of the ads two weeks ago. Asked if BT has objections to the ad, he said, "Potentially, yes.
"We are still considering our position," he said. "I can certainly confirm that we have written to Bell Cablemedia."

The spokesman said the letter sent to Bell Cablemedia was related to the ad, but he declined to say if Bell Cablemedia had responded. A time frame on any further action that may be taken by BT would depend on how Bell Cablemedia responds, he said.
"We're not commenting at all on the campaign," a spokeswoman for Bell Cablemedia, told Reuters.

A press release issued by Bell Cablemedia earlier this week said its advertising campaign is aimed "at the smart consumer: someone who is looking for the best value and most technologically advanced service from their telephone company." The ad campaign was designed by Rapier, Stead & Bowden.

Britain's phone market is open to any players, although BT continues to be the dominant provider. The market, however, has become increasingly competitive as new providers -- particularly cable television operators which can piggy-back phone service on their existing cable networks -- have entered the market.
